title: Smothered mate
line: A knight mates a king hemmed in by its own pieces.

steps.text: The black king is walled in by its own rook and pawns. Only a knight can check it here, because a knight jumps.

steps.hint: Find the knight jump that attacks the corner.
steps.after: Smothered mate. The king's own pieces take every square it could flee to.

steps.text: Here g8 is empty, so a knight check is not yet mate. A famous line chases the king and then gives the queen to fill g8.
Check with the knight from f7.
steps.hint: The knight jumps next to the black king.
steps.after: The king's only square is g8.

steps.text: Move the knight with check, and the queen checks too. Two checks at once is a double check: the king must move.
steps.hint: The knight leaves the queen's diagonal and checks from the edge.
steps.after: The king goes back to the corner. On f8 it would be mated by the queen on f7.

steps.text: Give the queen: check on g8. The knight guards it, so only the rook can take.
steps.hint: The queen goes to the corner of the king's box.
steps.after: The rook had to take, and now it stands on g8, walling in its own king.

steps.hint: Back to the square where the knight first gave check.

summary: A king walled in by its own pieces can be mated by a lone knight. A queen given up can build the wall.
